speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Our economic openness makes us attractive for investments and businesses, but also makes us an attractive target for money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I shall refer to these as "financial crimes" for convenience, throughout my speech.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As a trusted international financial and trading hub, Singapore takes a firm stance against these activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: We therefore take a robust approach to supervision, (a) both in the financial sector and non-financial sectors, (b) in order to prevent financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In 1992, Singapore joined the Financial Action Task Force, or FATF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The FATF is the recognised international standards setter for the prevention of financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Over 200 jurisdictions subscribe to the international FATF Standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Aside from the financial sector, the FATF has highlighted that other non-financial sectors also have an important role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This would include the following sectors which come under the Ministry of Law, or MinLaw’s purview: precious stones and precious metals dealers, or PSMDs; moneylending; pawnbroking; and legal services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As the regulator of these sectors, MinLaw regularly reviews our laws to ensure that they remain relevant, effective, and fully in line with the latest international standards set by the FATF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In recent years, the FATF has updated its standards, in particular, to set out clearly the identification, assessment and mitigation of risks associated with the financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, or “proliferation financing” in short.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will be achieved through proposed amendments to four Acts, namely: the Precious Stones and Precious Metals (Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing) Act, or the PSPM Act; the Moneylenders Act; the Pawnbrokers Act; and the Legal Profession Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, this Bill proposes amendments to the PSPM Act to strengthen the regulatory regime and enhance operational effectiveness in regulating PSMDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As a brief background, the PSPM Act was enacted in 2019 to provide a comprehensive regulatory and supervisory regime to prevent dealings in precious stones and precious metals from being used to facilitate money laundering or terrorism financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Since its enactment, MinLaw has continued to engage the PSMD sector for feedback and to review our measures and practices, emerging risks, global trends and developments and international standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The proposed amendments today are the culmination of these engagements and reviews.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: First, the Bill updates the PSPM Act, Moneylenders Act, Pawnbrokers Act and Legal Profession Act to clearly align the regulatory regime for the PSMD, moneylending, pawnbroking and legal services sectors with the updated FATF standards; and require businesses or persons covered by these Acts to implement adequate measures to counter proliferation financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Examples of required measures include: performing risk assessment; and developing and implementing internal policies, procedures, and controls to counter proliferation financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Such measures are not new to these businesses or persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For many entities, such measures are already part of their existing anti-money laundering controls as the underlying proliferation financing offences are also money laundering predicate offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, the controls in the Moneylenders Act and Pawnbrokers Act against criminals owning or managing moneylending and pawnbroking businesses will be strengthened, in line with the FATF Recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Second, the Bill strengthens the regulatory regime for PSMDs through amendments to the PSPM Act.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Bill seeks to update the definition of "precious product".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The PSPM Act covers precious stones and precious metals, or PSPM in short, and precious products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under the current definition, "precious product" means any jewellery, watch, apparel, accessory, ornament, or other finished product – made up of, containing, or having attached to it, any PSPM; and where at least 50% of the value of the product is attributable to the PSPM.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Based on the current definition, products with majority of value attributed to other factors, such as branding or workmanship, are not captured.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: However, we have observed that such products can also pose risks of financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: To illustrate, following the amendment, a platinum watch retailed by a luxury brand, with a net sales price of S$100,000, will be covered under the Act, even if the value of the platinum in the watch is less than 50% of the net sales price.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The prescribed threshold value of S$20,000 is aligned with FATF standards and international best practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Compliance officers are instrumental in the implementation of controls to prevent financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Therefore, the Bill makes it clear that compliance officers appointed by PSMDs must be assessed by the Registrar to be "fit and proper" persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition, the Bill will empower the Registrar to continue regulatory action against former registered PSMDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For instance, the Registrar may order them to pay financial penalties if they had failed to comply with the registration conditions, or if their registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 8 of the Bill amends section 10 to allow the Registrar to cancel or suspend the registration of PSMDs that are not conducting regulated dealing and/or fall under prescribed circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will mitigate the risk of PSMDs misusing their registration status to gain access to the financial system to conduct illicit transactions, or to create an erroneous impression that their businesses are regulated by MinLaw, for any purpose other than the prevention of financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 7 of the Bill introduces a new section 9A to provide that the registration of a registered PSMD lapses if the PSMD, as an entity, is wound up or otherwise dissolved, or if the PSMD, as a sole proprietor, dies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This will enable the Registrar to update the register more expeditiously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 19 of the Bill introduces new sections 36A and 36B in the PSPM Act to prescribe methods of service of documents required or authorised by the Act to be served on any person.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In particular, service through digital means will be prescribed to reduce the need for physical mail, better leverage technology and improve efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It will also reaffirm our strong commitment to be a responsible member of the international community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: With that Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on the Government’s approach on prevention of proliferation financing, anti-money laundering and counter terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Each of these areas represent risks which threaten the integrity of Singapore’s financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Each of these areas also have their own sets of safeguards and requirements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore has a national strategy for countering terrorism financing related activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Senior Parliamentary Secretary share if proliferation financing will be incorporated into this strategy?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share how the Government is incorporating these safeguards as a coherent approach to prevent fragmentation in the implementation of the financial safeguards for proliferation financing, money laundering and terrorism financing?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification is on ensuring effective implementation of these safeguards on the ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Robust safeguards are important due to the seriousness of the threat posed by proliferation financing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, overly strict safeguards can be counter-productive if entities do not have the capacity to ensure meaningful compliance with these safeguards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What steps will be taken at the industry level to avoid these safeguards from becoming a box-checking exercise?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The proposed amendments to the said Acts add to the existing provisions in respect of prevention of money laundering and prevention of terrorism financing.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In August last year, the Singapore Police Force (SPF) arrested 10 foreigners holding multiple citizenships for alleged money laundering offences involving cash, luxury properties, cars, gold bars, handbags, jewellery, branded watches and cryptocurrency, including more than 68 gold bars, 294 luxury bags, 164 branded watches and 546 pieces of jewellery we are told.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In October 2023, we were told that 152 properties and 62 vehicles were involved, and we were told last month that 55 new properties and 15 vehicles were given prohibition of disposal orders by the police.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Minister Josephine Teo had said that the proceeds "most likely came from criminal activities abroad, including illegal online gambling and unlicensed moneylending".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The inability of our existing laws and regulations to prevent the current money laundering case is worrying.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Has any lesson been applied to today’s amendments?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How have our existing laws or regulations failed to stop the accused persons from bringing into Singapore, funds which have been the subject of money laundering and/or from proceeds of organised crime activities and to be allowed to invest such funds in different ways in Singapore such as buying properties?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Has the Government started reviewing the existing laws and if not, whether and when it will do so?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: These are highly relevant to today’s Bill as we are seeking to apply the current suite of laws and regulations against the financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and we need to be assured that the current laws or the proposed amendments can provide adequate gatekeeping to prevent entry to Singapore of funds for financing of proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also hope that the authorities will review the adequacy of the due diligence efforts of banks, law firms and other professionals or stakeholders who were involved in respect of the funds brought in by the said foreign nationals in the ongoing money laundering case or in respect of funds used for the purchases of different properties and to consider what laws, regulations and measures need to be enhanced to strengthen the current due diligence process required of all professionals and stakeholders and hopefully minimise the risks of such cases recurring, which is embarrassing for our country and tarnishes Singapore’s reputation as a financial centre.
, "That the Bill be now read a Second time." –  .

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, amidst these positive strides, I have some clarifications about the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, we must ensure that the expanded regulations are implemented effectively and fairly, balancing our needs to counter illicit finance with the well-being of small businesses, like small-and-medium sized enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Registrar ensure that the new powers over former registered dealers and recordkeeping are not abused?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Registrar receive additional resources to handle the expanded scope and powers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the obligations on legal professionals, pawnbrokers and moneylenders be implemented?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In particular, small businesses like SMEs could be disproportionately affected by the compliance costs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What education or support will be provided to newly regulated businesses like jewellers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, auditors, accountants and other professionals impacted by the proposed Act requires adequate training and time to digest the new regulations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I urge the Government to grant sufficient lead time for this critical adaptation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I wish to seek clarification on managing the emerging risks within our framework.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister clarify the current status of our engagement with the FATF, regarding the remaining gaps in the framework?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the next milestones that we can look forward to?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, the growing field of fintech presents novel challenges, particularly with virtual assets and crowdfunding platforms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What specific measures are being considered to manage the risks associated with these evolving technologies?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are additional regulations under consideration to prevent these avenues from becoming havens for illegal activity?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Does the Ministry conduct regular reviews of money laundering and terrorism financing risks within our borders?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Sharing the current landscape of top threats will allow us to stay ahead of the curve and refine our defences accordingly.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I have queries about the effectiveness of existing controls.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What specific safeguards are currently in place to curb illicit activities?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How can we improve collaboration to further strengthen our defences?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While we must remain thoughtful of potential regulatory overreach, the new powers conferred upon the Registrar are judiciously scoped and proportionate to the risks at hand.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The transitional arrangements also demonstrate pragmatism in avoiding excessive disruption to businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill signifies our commitment to safeguarding the integrity of Singapore's financial system against illicit activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must persist in this journey of continuous improvement, while balancing commercial interests and staying ahead of sophisticated criminal networks.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am confident that the measures in this Bill will strengthen our defences against money laundering, terrorism and proliferation financing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us act swiftly and collectively to ensure that illegal financing finds no refuge in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In recent years, Singapore has ramped up its efforts to counter financial crimes in various sectors including precious metals and precious stones.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill demonstrates Singapore's dynamic regulatory approach which fortifies the legal framework while emphasising regulatory compliance, international collaboration and the importance of transparent and ethical practices.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Though the Bill focuses on diverse professions from legal, moneylending and pawnbroking to sectors such as precious stones and precious metals, the benefits will be similar in nature for all.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Through this amended Bill, businesses operating within these sectors will be able to differentiate themselves in the market by demonstrating a strong commitment to preventing money laundering and the financing of terrorism and, in turn, can enhance a company's reputation through building trust with its customers, partners and regulators.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: By adhering to the updated regulations and increasing internal controls, businesses within these sectors can mitigate the risk of being involved in illicit activities unknowingly.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: I also believe that the facilitation of information sharing with foreign authorities presents an opportunity for our businesses to engage in more robust international collaboration.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This can lead to better global practices and potentially open new markets and partnerships that value such stringent compliance standards.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: This Bill also extends the regulatory burden to a broader range of professional services, not just financial institutions.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: For the legal profession, I expect legal practitioners and law firms will now be required to take active measures in monitoring transactions to prevent financial crimes.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The pawnbroking industry will also need to establish more robust programmes to prevent financial crimes.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: The amended Bill requires the development of policies to identify, assess, and understand risks associated with such pawnbroking transactions.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Also, what additional resources or assistance programmes will the Government provide to help affected businesses understand as well as comply with the new regulations?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: Could I please request the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to share with this House any instances thus far that Singapore’s security and policing authorities have faced in detecting efforts to use precious stones and metals in financing terrorism?

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: In offering a stable and transparent business environment, we have attracted multinationals and investors from around the world.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: They have set up corporate headquarters and regional offices in Singapore, building up our talent and business ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: We must continue to stay abreast of international developments to counter threats such as money laundering, terrorism financing, as well as other financial crimes.

speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
text: To do so, we need robust policies and coordination within sectors to build capabilities in businesses, especially local SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Members also made comments and suggestions on Singapore's national strategy for preventing money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation financing or "financial crimes", and the scope and implementation of the expanded regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: First, on Singapore’s national strategy for preventing financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Ng asked about our strategies in managing these risks and how agencies work together to ensure that our system effectively guards against these risks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore's openness and hub status leave us vulnerable to exploitation by criminals who employ sophisticated tactics to access our financial and trading system and launder their ill-gotten gains.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We must constantly review and enhance our regime and defences to keep pace with new risks as they evolve.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore adopts a holistic approach across the Government, in partnership with the private sector, and through international collaboration to combat financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Ministry of Law (MinLaw) is a member of this committee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Specific to the inter-agency coordination between regulators and law enforcement that Mr Yip asked about, an example is the Risk and Typologies Inter-Agency Group (RTIG), which is co-chaired by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It oversees the identification, assessment, and mitigation of financial crime risks at the whole-of-Government level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The RTIG involves all relevant supervisory and law enforcement agencies, including the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Office.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It also facilitates the sharing of information on surveillance outputs, such as networks and subjects of concern, for collective action across law enforcement and supervisory agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond coordinating within the Government, there is also close collaboration between Government agencies and the private sector to prevent, detect and deter activities in relation to financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An example is the AML/CFT Industry Partnership (ACIP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Co-chaired by MAS and the Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) of the Singapore Police Force (SPF), ACIP brings selected industry participants, regulators, law enforcement agencies and other Government entities to identify, assess and mitigate key and emerging financial crime risks that Singapore is facing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Another example of close public-private partnership is MinLaw's industry engagements with the precious stones and precious metals dealers (PSMD) industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MinLaw has also taken steps through industry bodies to help PSMDs better understand and implement the relevant regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to ensure strong coordination and collaboration across agencies, work closely with the private sector and our international partners and effectively guard against illicit activities related to financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip asked about the current status of our engagement with FATF, whether there are remaining gaps in the framework and the next milestones we can look forward to.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore was evaluated by the FATF in 2016 and was assessed to have a strong legal and institutional framework against money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have since taken substantial steps to address the few areas identified with scope for improvement and further strengthened our regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, Singapore passed the PSPM Act of 2019 and amended the Accountants Act to give the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) the powers to conduct inspections for compliance with requirements to combat money laundering and terrorism financing and impose sanctions on entities if they fail to comply with these requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These ongoing efforts were acknowledged by the FATF and had raised some of Singapore's ratings in the Third Follow Up Report of 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore also actively contributes to the FATF, having taken on a range of leadership roles over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through Singapore's ongoing FATF Presidency, we have, among other things, increased global effectiveness of measures against financial crimes, such as in beneficial ownership transparency and asset recovery, and raised international efforts on tackling emerging areas of financial crime risks such as cyber-enabled fraud, which further strengthen global resilience against financial crime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked whether this Bill factors in lessons from the recent money laundering case and whether the Government has started reviewing existing laws to better prevent money laundering in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MinLaw's review of issues in the current Bill started prior to the arrest of the suspects involved in the recent money laundering case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is part of MinLaw's regular reviews to ensure that our laws remain relevant, effective and fully in line with the latest international standards set by the FATF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On the recent money laundering case, investigations by the Police are still ongoing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are also ongoing probes by various sectoral regulators, including Government agencies overseeing corporate service providers, real estate agents, PSMDs, lawyers, financial institutions and others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Committee is currently reviewing the adequacies of the laws and controls in the entire anti-money laundering ecosystem to assess whether there are areas of enhancements to be made.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Committee will put forward its recommendations when ready.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Next, I turn to the questions relating to the scope and implementation of the expanded regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether the requirements for PSMD, moneylending, pawnbroking and legal services sectors to implement measures to counter proliferation financing might result in excessive compliance burden on these businesses or persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As mentioned in my opening speech for this Bill, these requirements are not expected to result in significant compliance implications on the regulated entities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The measures to counter proliferation financing are similar to the measures that the PSMD, moneylending, pawnbroking and legal services sectors already have in place to counter money laundering and terrorism financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked for the steps taken at the industry level to prevent the safeguards from becoming a box-checking exercise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MinLaw requires the entities it regulates to develop and implement measures to prevent financial crimes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We also carry out inspections, investigations and enforcement to ensure compliance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Neil Parekh and Mr Yip asked about the education or support that will be provided to the regulated entities to help them understand and comply with the new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Parekh also asked about key concerns raised by pawnbrokers and PSMDs in relation to this Bill and how much time the regulated entities will be given to implement these new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MinLaw will continue to engage the relevant sectors as the changes are rolled out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will also provide guidance for the regulated entities to comply with the new requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While no major concerns have been raised during consultations, MinLaw will continue working with industry associations as the new requirements are implemented and, at the same time, having a view to the compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Should MinLaw come across regulated entities that are not complying with the requirements after the amendments are in force, we will assess and follow up with them to rectify the situation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will take into consideration the time that regulated entities may reasonably need to implement these measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip asked about the requirement for former regulated dealers to continue keeping records for a prescribed period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The intention of this requirement is to deter errant PSMDs from disposing of records after ceasing to be regulated dealers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The new provision will allow enforcement action to be taken against former regulated dealers, for example, if they dispose of records to thwart investigations into offences under the PSPM Act detected while they were regulated dealers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Investigations for complex cases may take longer and extend beyond the dealer's registration period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Hence, it is important to preserve these records as evidence to assist in investigations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Registrar will exercise his powers of investigations provided under the PSPM Act judiciously.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MinLaw will also continually review the regulatory and enforcement resources to leverage technology where possible and work closely with stakeholders in the process.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There were a number of other comments relating to matters outside the ambit of the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked about instances where Singapore's security and policing authorities have detected efforts to use precious stones and metals in financing terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To date, there has been no indication of the PSMD sector in Singapore being used to finance terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore closely monitors developments in the methods used by terrorists and remains vigilant in combating the threat of terrorism financing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip asked about the specific measures that are being considered to manage risks associated with evolving technologies in the field of fintech.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Criminal typologies and methods will continue to change in line with developments and advances in technology and we must keep pace with these changes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We regularly review and update our framework to counter activities in relation to financial crimes as criminals innovate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, when virtual assets, or what we term as digital assets, took off years ago, MAS had assessed the risk of financial crimes as a key area of concern due to the potential of digital assets to facilitate rapid and anonymous transactions online and across borders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Yip also asked about the effectiveness and safeguards in relation to casinos' anti-money laundering controls since 2006.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) requires the casino operators to put in place safeguards to prevent money laundering, such as conducting customer due diligence checks and periodic monitoring of patrons' transactions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any Members who have clarifications to seek from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu?
